title: Constant etale direct image across a regular normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $B$ a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, $Y$ a regular Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] on which $\ell$ is invertible, and $D\subseteq Y$ a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $j:Y\setminus D\hookrightarrow Y$ be the complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $r$ be the number of irreducible components of $D$. On the ordinary small etale sites, all the sheaves $R^qj_*B_{Y\setminus D}$ are constructible, and $R^qj_*B_{Y\setminus D}=0$ for $q>r$. Thus $Rj_*B_{Y\setminus D}\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The empty boundary is allowed, with $r=0$.

source.place: XVI Corollary 3.1.3 (normal-crossings exterior-algebra formula), deduced there from Theorem 3.1.1; XIII Proposition 3.6.2. Finite-field coefficients follow by the finite free scalar extension from F_ell to B.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. We prove the following strengthened induction assertion for every $m\geq0$, simultaneously for all integers $t$: if $X$ is regular Noetherian with $\ell$ invertible and $C_1,\ldots,C_m$ are closed regular subschemes whose every nonempty indexed intersection $C_J$ is regular with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}-\dim\mathcal O_{C_J,x}=|J|$ at each of its points, then, for $u:X-\bigcup_iC_i\hookrightarrow X$, $Ru_*A(t)$ has constructible cohomology in degrees $[0,m]$ only. Empty or disconnected $C_i$ and empty intersections are allowed. The given boundary supplies exactly this intersection condition by [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. For $m=0$, $u$ is the identity and $A_X(t)$ is a finite locally constant rank-one sheaf by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; hence the assertion holds. For any $m$, negative higher direct images of a sheaf vanish: the bounded-below injective resolution defining [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] can start in degree zero.

source.place: XVI Corollary 3.1.3; agent strengthening for the induction, including the empty boundary

proof.text:
We will use tensor transport only for the invertible Tate line $L=A_X(t)$, whose inverse is $A_X(-t)$: evaluation is an isomorphism since on a trivializing etale cover it is multiplication $A\otimes_AA\to A$. For any scheme morphism $f:T\to X$ and any derived $E$, the derived adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and the monoidal inverse image of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,Rf_*E\otimes L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N\otimes L^{-1},Rf_*E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}N\otimes f^{-1}L^{-1},E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,Rf_*(E\otimes f^{-1}L)).$$
Thus $Rf_*E\otimes L\cong Rf_*(E\otimes f^{-1}L)$: the maps corresponding to identities under these natural bijections are inverse. In particular, for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ the same calculation applies to its direct image. All tensors here are derived; tensoring by a Tate line is also termwise exact because locally it is the identity functor.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; formal invertible-line case of the adjunction, written out

proof.text:
For a regular codimension-one closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ between regular Noetherian schemes, [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] ensures that it is a regular immersion; the length of a local regular sequence generating the ideal at $z$ equals $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z}-\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}=1$, since each element of a regular sequence lowers the local dimension by one. So [lem-per-gabber-regular-pair-purity] with $n=1,c=1$ gives $i^!A_X\cong A_Z(-1)[-2]$, without excellence. The exceptional functor here is the right adjoint of $i_*$ in [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]: in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] choose the identity open followed by the proper closed immersion, so $Ri_!=Ri_*$. By the finite exactness and module-forgetting comparisons in step 7, $i_*$ is exact on module sheaves. Hence for every complex $K$ and K-injective resolution $K\to I$, termwise $i_*$ keeps the acyclic cone acyclic, so $i_*K\to i_*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism: the unbounded $Ri_*$ is termwise $i_*$ on all of $D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and the two right adjoints agree. For the Tate line $L=A_X(t)$, the preceding tensor transport and the adjunction $i_*\dashv i^!$ give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,i^!A_X\otimes i^{-1}L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*(M\otimes i^{-1}L^{-1}),A_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*M,A_X\otimes L).$$
The inverse maps represented by identities therefore give $i^!(A_X(t))\cong A_Z(t-1)[-2]$. The pullback and tensor identifications of Tate lines are those of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For empty $Z$, both supported terms are zero.

source.place: XVI Theorem 3.1.1, codimension one; agent-written invertible-line adjunction calculation

proof.text: Assume the assertion of step 1 for $m-1$ and all integer twists. Write $C=C_m$, $V=X-\bigcup_{i<m}C_i$, $U=V-C$, and use immersions $v:V\hookrightarrow X$, $b:U\hookrightarrow V$, $a:E=C\cap V\hookrightarrow V$, $i:C\hookrightarrow X$, $k:E\hookrightarrow C$. Then $u=vb$ and $va=ik$. The schemes $V,E$ are regular Noetherian, because their local rings are those of $X,C$. The immersion $a$ has codimension one. On $C$, the family $C\cap C_i$ for $i<m$ satisfies the induction hypothesis: its indexed intersections are $C_{J\cup\{m\}}$, and subtracting the dimension equality for $C$ from that for $C_{J\cup\{m\}}$ gives codimension $|J|$ in $C$. These intersections are regular by assumption; [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] makes their immersions regular. They may be disconnected, which is why the induction assertion did not require irreducibility. Thus the induction hypothesis applies both to $v$ on $X$ and to $k$ on $C$.

source.place: XVI Corollary 3.1.3; agent divisor-deletion induction and intersection bookkeeping

proof.text:
Apply the closed-support triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] on $V$ to $K=A_V(t)$ and to the closed/open pair $(a,b)$. Substitute the codimension-one purity calculation of step 3. This gives the distinguished triangle
$$a_*A_E(t-1)[-2]\longrightarrow A_V(t)\longrightarrow Rb_*A_U(t)\longrightarrow a_*A_E(t-1)[-1].$$
All objects are ordinary etale $A$-module complexes. In particular, the purity theorem is applied to the regular pair $(V,E)$, and never to the possibly singular union of boundary components.

source.place: XVI Theorem 3.1.1 applied to (V,E); localization triangle supplied by lem-exc-closed-support-triangle

proof.text:
Apply $Rv_*$ to this triangle; it preserves distinguished triangles and shifts by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The derived direct-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], first for $vb=u$ and then for $va=ik$, identifies the resulting triangle as
$$i_*Rk_*A_E(t-1)[-2]\longrightarrow Rv_*A_V(t)\longrightarrow Ru_*A_U(t)\longrightarrow i_*Rk_*A_E(t-1)[-1].$$
Here $Ra_*=a_*$ and $Ri_*=i_*$ on the bounded-below inputs by the finite exactness and module comparison of step 7. All indexing sites are small representatives of ordinary small etale sites, and all coefficients are the same constant ring $A$; hence the composition theorem's ringed-topos hypotheses hold.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; derived exactness of additive direct image

proof.text: Closed immersions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. For such a map, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exact direct image on abelian sheaves; [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the underlying abelian higher direct images of module sheaves with those abelian higher direct images. Consequently module higher direct images vanish in positive degrees, and direct image is exact on modules (exactness is checked after forgetting the action). A bounded-below resolution therefore gives $Ri_*=i_*$ and $\mathcal H^q(i_*M)=i_*\mathcal H^q(M)$. If $F$ is a constructible $A$-module sheaf on $C$, [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] puts it in the source library's constructibility notion. Its stalks are finite, since each is a finite-dimensional vector space over finite $A$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-finite-stalk-module], with Noetherian target $X$, says $i_*F$ is constructible. This proves the constructibility and degree preservation needed for the first term of step 6, and proves the identical exactness assertion for $a$.

source.place: Tag 095R, lemma-finite-pushforward-constructible; module finite-stalk and forgetting comparisons cited explicitly

proof.text:
By induction, $Rv_*A_V(t)$ and $Rk_*A_E(t-1)$ have constructible cohomology in degrees $[0,m-1]$. Hence the first term of step 6 has constructible cohomology in degrees $[2,m+1]$ by step 7. In the cohomology sequence of that triangle [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], the segment
$$\mathcal H^q(Rv_*A_V(t))\longrightarrow\mathcal H^q(Ru_*A_U(t))\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal H^{q-1}(Rk_*A_E(t-1))$$
shows vanishing of the middle sheaf for $q>m$. Its negative cohomology is zero by step 1. More precisely the middle sheaf is an extension of the cokernel of the preceding arrow into $\mathcal H^q(Rv_*A_V(t))$ by the kernel of the following arrow out of $i_*\mathcal H^{q-1}(Rk_*A_E(t-1))$. All four surrounding terms are constructible. Kernels, cokernels and extensions are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. This completes the induction. Applying it to the $r$ boundary components and $t=0$ proves the item for $A=\mathbf F_\ell$.

source.place: XIII Proposition 3.6.2 and XVI Corollary 3.1.3; explicit degree bound by localization induction

proof.text: Finally choose an $A$-basis of the finite field $B$, of dimension $d$. The underlying abelian sheaf of $B_U$ is $A_U^{\oplus d}$. For every integer $q$, [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison], applied once for $B$ and once for $A$, identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qj_*B_U$ with $(R^qj_*A_U)^{\oplus d}$, because the additive derived abelian direct image preserves finite biproducts. Thus it vanishes for $q\notin[0,r]$. For each remaining $q$, choose the finite constructible stratification supplied by the result over $A$. On each stratum the latter finite biproduct has finite locally constant underlying sets. Apply [lem-pod-module-local-constancy-of-finite-underlying] to the restricted $B$-module sheaf: it is locally constant as a module sheaf, and its values are finite because their underlying sets are finite. Therefore $R^qj_*B_U$ is constructible in the definition of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The same definition gives $Rj_*B_U\in D^b_c$ with cohomology in $[0,r]$. For $D=\varnothing$, $j$ is the identity, so this specializes to $B_Y$ in degree zero, including the empty ambient scheme.

source.place: Finite free scalar extension from F_ell to B; XVI Corollary 3.1.3 and the definition of bounded constructibility
